item.title: 37% of AI time savings eroded by need to review and revise outputs
item.description: While AI has increased gross productivity, net gains have been eroded by the time and effort needed to review and correct AI outputs.

item.title: Despite high-profile defection, Merrill says advisor exits at record low
item.description: Bank of America's wealth management businesses suffered a blow last year when principals of a team that managed $130 billion in AUM left for independence. Merrill executives are now looking to the future with ambitious recruiting and cross-selling plans.

item.title: Net new assets stall at Citi Wealth following Q4 drop
item.description: A sharp fourth-quarter decline in net new investment assets weighed on Citi's wealth division, tempering full-year growth despite revenue gains.

item.title: RIAs that don't invest in marketing aren't growing organically, study says
item.description: An organic growth technology firm launched out of Fidelity Investment's incubator spoke with 18 big RIAs about their marketing. The results speak for themselves.

item.title: Raymond James to acquire $46B Clark Capital Management
item.description: Philadelphia-based Clark Capital will be one of several "boutique" firms in Raymond James' global asset management division.

item.title: Private credit drops safeguard to win deals on Wall Street terms
item.description: Once rare, the same kind of permissive terms that are widespread on leveraged loans are becoming increasingly common in the $1.7 trillion private credit market.

item.title: Parental leave stress-tests a practice. Here's how advisors make it work
item.description: Clear and early communication, with coworkers as well as clients, is key when planning for a long leave.

item.title: Morgan Stanley barrels toward $10T as new assets more than double in Q4
item.description: The wealth management giant capped off 2025 by pressing ever closer to the asset and wealth management target set by former CEO James Gorman.

item.title: Goldman's stock traders beat their own Wall Street record
item.description: Goldman Sachs shattered expectations with a record $4.31 billion in fourth-quarter equities trading revenue, topping its own Wall Street high set just months earlier.

item.title: How dual share classes could reshape the future of ETFs
item.description: Regulators officially approved 30 more funds last month, with more expected authorizations in 2026. Will financial advisors and their clients bite?
